parsed.explanation: The traveller-facing exposure sits mostly in the parent regime: visa/entry screening instructs refusal where documents cast 'reasonable doubt' on sex, with fraud-referral risking lifetime ineligibility; foreign governments have issued travel advisories; a federal facilities ban excludes trans people from government-funded single-sex spaces; and immigration/federal custody carries documented patterned abuse (forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse, hormone removal) with no shown remedy — a severe, state-perpetrated pipeline for anyone detained. Offsetting this: the division has no facility ban in force (the bill died), no criminalisation of trans presentation, no organised targeting or documented trans-specific violence, a gender-identity hate-crime aggravator, and functioning courts that have blocked several national measures (while upholding the passport rule). Social climate is conservative. Universal document/entry exposure plus conditional custody severity place this at the top of Elevated Risk, below unremedied ward/custody placement cases.
